title: World Bank Enterprise Survey: Philippines 2023 (public source)
summary: World Bank survey of formal private firms with five or more employees on their business environment, including bank accounts, how they finance investment and their biggest obstacles.
label_notes: Pages are 1-based PDF page indexes. Values come from the appendix table (pp.11-12), whose columns are Philippines 2023 all firms, small, medium, large, then East Asia & Pacific and lower-middle-income comparators. Small-firm base (424) is from Figure 2 (p.4).

findings.text: 79.8% of formal private firms in the Philippines had a checking or savings account.
findings.quote: Percent of firms with a checking or savings account 79.8

findings.text: Among small firms (5-19 employees), 78.2% had a checking or savings account.
findings.quote: Percent of firms with a checking or savings account 79.8 78.2

findings.text: Firms financed 68.0% of their investment internally; banks financed 19.8%.
findings.quote: Proportion of investment financed by banks (%) 19.8

findings.text: 28.9% of firms used banks to finance investments.
findings.quote: Percent of firms using banks to finance investments 28.9

findings.text: Access to finance was named the biggest business obstacle by 12.8% of firms, third after electricity (18.1%) and practices of the informal sector (13.6%).
Only 15% of small firms had a bank loan, against 31% of medium and 37% of large firms.
